quotes.text: Stripe no longer recommends using the Card Element as part of your Web Elements integration.
They only need to authenticate their account once every 90 days on any Link-enabled business.
The Payment Request Button is deprecated and isn’t supported in Stripe.js `endive` or later.
In production, Link's visibility might vary to maximize Link's conversion benefits in each checkout session.

old_evidence.text: Link in the Card Element operates independently from Link in the Payment Request button.
Typically, we require a minimum width of 350px and height of 28px.

findings: The Card Element remains documented for existing integrations and is no longer recommended in both captures. November replaces the preferred Link Authentication Element with Contact Details Element and keeps Express Checkout Element and Payment Element (old raw lines 6-12,130-134, new raw lines 7-13,131-135). This recommendation does not establish a rename, interoperability, or removal of either Card Element or Link Authentication Element. The separate Payment Request Button is explicitly deprecated and unsupported on Stripe.js `endive` or later, with qualified continued support on earlier supported versions and Express Checkout Element migration guidance (old raw lines 61-63, new raw lines 62-64). Keep the dated version limit with reciprocal Link and Payment Request Button routes. The separate November Button capture corroborates it at raw/stripe-payments-link-payment-request-button-link-2026-11-07.md:5-13. The retained npm package summary documents Endive loader/type changes without removing the lower-level `stripe.paymentRequest` API (wiki/sources/stripe/github/source-github-stripe-js.md:369-377).

Baseline source lines 21-33 summarize shared behavior across single and split Card Elements, but the 350×28 px guidance is typical, conditioned on font, locale, placeholder and icon visibility (old raw lines 51-59, new raw lines 52-60). Automatic enablement is for granted-access accounts, excludes India-based Stripe accounts as captured and is distinct from actual display. Production may selectively render Link, whereas an enabled sandbox shows it on eligible sessions. Pop-up support is required and COOP `same-origin` blocks the necessary opener communication (old raw lines 33-59,109-128, new raw lines 34-60,110-129). Carry these qualifications in the reciprocal Link concept (wiki/concepts/stripe-link.md:122-128,180).

Both captures describe separate eligibility for receiving Link via Connect and controlling Link settings. Connected accounts can manage their own settings if the platform uses direct charges, creates and charges payment methods on connected accounts, and the accounts have full Dashboard access. Cloned platform payment methods, destination charges, separate charges and transfers, or absence of full Dashboard access leave control with the platform. Distinguish payments through the platform from payments processed without it. `disableLink` can selectively disable for specific accounts where the platform controls settings (old raw lines 65-107, new raw lines 66-108). The general automatic availability sentence does not displace the separate granted-access/India qualifications or guarantee per-session production display.

Both guides describe Link sign-up via email, phone and payment method, or saving a card entered first, and authenticated buyers using Link to autofill saved details. Returning buyers can be prompted for SMS or email verification and the guides describe an authentication window of 90 days across Link-enabled businesses. Production selectivity still applies, and authentication/autofill is not a PaymentIntent confirmation or proof of a successful charge (old raw lines 14-43,128, new raw lines 15-44,129).

Both dates retain the supported browser list, grant-qualified production and sandbox and fixed sandbox codes. The special test errors distinguish invalid, expired and maximum attempts. Stripe cautions against real user data in sandbox Link accounts because they are associated with the publishable key (old raw lines 109-128, new raw lines 110-129).
substantive_changes: November recommends Contact Details Element in place of Link Authentication Element for this migration decision, with corresponding See also route change (old raw lines 6-12,130-134, new raw lines 7-13,131-135).

November adds the Payment Request Button's explicit deprecation, unsupported Stripe.js `endive` or later boundary, conditional earlier-version support and migration route while retaining independent Link behavior if both appear in a supported earlier integration (old raw lines 61-63, new raw lines 62-64).

Both snapshots preserve the 2023 single-line release and late 2023/early 2024 split release, grant/India qualifications, dimensions, popup/COOP, per-platform controls and sandbox/production behavior (old raw lines 2-12,45-128, new raw lines 46-129).

The screenshot URLs, formatting, step numbering, punctuation and table spacing changes are presentation. The new migration recommendation and version constraint have independent semantic content (old raw lines 18-29,61-63,79-99,121-126, new raw lines 19-30,62-64,80-100,122-127).

source_assessments.reason: New replacement guidance and an SDK-train boundary require source updates. Existing Card Element deprecation and display wording independently require qualification.

answers.Q1: The November 7 capture of https://docs.stripe.com/payments/link/card-element-link describes Link sign-up, verification and autofill with single-line and split Card Elements. Returning customers may be asked for SMS or email verification and the guide describes a 90-day authentication window. An enabled Card Element can show Link to granted-access accounts, with an India exclusion, browser pop-up support, opener communication and typically 350 by 28 pixel container guidance. An eligible sandbox displays Link when enabled and production may vary. Dashboard disablement and disableLink are separate controls. For Connect, direct charges, creating and charging payment methods on connected accounts and full Dashboard access permit account settings control. Otherwise the platform controls platform payments in the listed cases (old raw lines 14-59, old raw lines 65-128, new raw lines 15-60 and new raw lines 66-129). source-stripe-card-element-link.md captures much of the May behavior. November instead recommends Contact Details Element alongside Express Checkout Element and Payment Element and explicitly excludes the separate Payment Request Button from Endive or later (old raw lines 6-12, old raw lines 61-63, new raw lines 7-13 and new raw lines 62-64). Link sign-up, successful verification or display does not prove completed payment.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/link/card-element-link, November changes preferred migration guidance from Link Authentication Element to Contact Details Element, and describes the separate Payment Request Button as deprecated and unsupported in Stripe.js Endive or later. Both Link surfaces can still appear independently while using an earlier supported version. The recommendation change does not establish a rename or technical Card Element removal (old raw lines 6-12, old raw lines 61-63, new raw lines 7-13 and new raw lines 62-64). Scope the version warning and conditional coexistence reciprocally in Stripe Link and its separate Payment Request Button route. source-stripe-card-element-link.md should preserve May provenance and earlier advice as dated. Changes to screenshot links, formatting, numbering and table spacing are presentation, with no new Connect, browser or sandbox behavior (old raw lines 18-29, old raw lines 65-128, new raw lines 19-30 and new raw lines 66-129). Keep eligibility separate from selective production visibility, typical size guidance from absolute thresholds, and authentication and autofill from a live payment outcome. The November SDK boundary concerns the Button Element and does not establish removal of the lower-level paymentRequest API.
